answer: A bond of 22% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in voyage, and harbor reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, someone cannot recycle one pool of capital across 196 aliases, and each one needs its own funded plume account. Each duplicate costs another 13 dollars in locked collateral and another 10 days of waiting. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
